name: Kiawah Island
intro: Kiawah is a private, gated island, so a ride there involves gate access as well as the drive.
facts: Kiawah Island's main gate and second Vanderhorst Gate are run by the Kiawah Island Community Association and staffed 24 hours a day by its security department.

The Association's commercial access page says businesses must buy a one-day or annual gate pass before entering, and drivers need a license, vehicle registration and insurance. Its listed one-day rate is $12 for four-wheel vehicles.
Kiawah Island Golf Resort puts Charleston International Airport about 32 miles and 40 to 45 minutes from the resort.
The island's tourism site describes Kiawah as about 21 miles south of historic Charleston, roughly 35 minutes by car.

name: Seabrook Island
intro: Seabrook Island has its own security gate, and vehicles behind it must display a gate pass.
facts: Behind the SIPOA security gate, vehicles must display a valid SIPOA gate pass at all times, and the speed limit is 25 mph unless posted otherwise.
Visitors arriving during the Daily Pass Office's hours are asked to stop at 1900 Seabrook Island Road for a pass; when it is closed they go directly to the Main Gate.
SIPOA gate data shows weekend visitor arrivals peak from 2 pm to 8 pm, at times averaging over 100 vehicles per hour.

name: Charleston
intro: Charleston International Airport regulates the ground transportation operators that serve it.
facts: Ground transportation at Charleston International Airport is governed by a Ground Transportation Services Ordinance that sets rules for operators at the terminal building.
The airport's transportation page says transporter vehicles must be properly equipped for passenger safety and appropriately insured.
Kiawah Island's tourism site describes the island as about 21 miles south of historic Charleston.
